public.prompt: A notebook cell calls `sns.set_theme(style='whitegrid', palette='deep')` and then draws a seaborn bar chart. The next cell draws a plain matplotlib line chart without calling `sns.set_theme()` again. What will the matplotlib line chart look like?

options.text: It will use the whitegrid style and deep palette, because `sns.set_theme()` changes global matplotlib rcParams that affect all subsequent plots.
It will use default matplotlib styling, because `sns.set_theme()` only affects seaborn plots.
It will raise an error, because `sns.set_theme()` must be called before every plot.
The seaborn bar chart will be restyled to match the matplotlib defaults.

opt_correct.message: Correct. `sns.set_theme()` changes the global defaults for all plots using the matplotlib rcParams system, so it affects matplotlib plots too, even ones not made with seaborn.

opt_default.message: `sns.set_theme()` does not only affect seaborn plots. It changes the global matplotlib rcParams, so all subsequent plots — including plain matplotlib ones — use the new style.

opt_error.message: `sns.set_theme()` does not need to be called before every plot. Once called, it changes the global rcParams, which persist for all subsequent plots in the session.

opt_retroactive.message: `sns.set_theme()` changes defaults for plots drawn after the call — it does not go back and restyle a figure you already drew and displayed earlier.

correct.message: Right. `sns.set_theme()` works by changing matplotlib's global rcParams, so it affects every plot drawn after the call — seaborn or not.

incorrect.message: `sns.set_theme()` changes the global matplotlib rcParams. Because it changes global defaults, all plots drawn after the call — including plain matplotlib plots — use the new style.

hints: Think about what 'global defaults' means — once changed, they apply to everything drawn afterward.
`sns.set_theme()` works through matplotlib's rcParams system, not a seaborn-only mechanism.
